output.review_comment:
The mixed-case-preservation and first/last-small-word fixes (rules 1 and 2) correctly implement what the docstring describes, and I traced through tests 1–7 and 9 — they all pass for reasons consistent with the documented rules.

However, `test_subtitle_after_colon` only passes because of the new `after_colon` tracking, and that behavior is not in the docstring at all. The docstring explicitly says a small word is capitalized "unless it is the first or the last word of `text`" — nothing about words following a colon. For "notes from the field: a year of remote work", "a" is neither the first nor last word of the whole string, yet the code now capitalizes it solely to satisfy the colon test. That's a rule invented to make one test pass, and it was added without updating the docstring to describe it.

Since the teammate was explicit that "the docstrings are the source of truth for how this code should behave," this PR leaves the docstring and the implementation out of sync: a reader of the docstring would not predict this subtitle-after-colon capitalization, and there's no comment or doc update explaining it. Please either:
1. Update the docstring to explicitly document the after-colon rule (so behavior and docs agree), or
2. Flag to the teammate that `test_subtitle_after_colon` conflicts with the documented rules as written, since the docstring doesn't currently support that expected output.

Right now the code "passes tests" but doesn't match its own documentation, which is the opposite of what was asked for.
